notes.front: What is the Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet?
notes.back: Form 13614-C: a tool that helps tax-law-certified volunteers ask the questions needed to prepare an accurate return.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 likens it to what a professional preparer or tax software asks of a taxpayer.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2: Intake Process, Step 4”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Form 13614-C, is a tool designed to assist IRS-tax law certified volunteers ask questions to obtain the information needed to prepare an accurate tax return. It is similar to what is required when a taxpayer visits a professional tax preparer or uses tax preparation software.
notes.example: Like a doctor’s new-patient questionnaire that the doctor then goes through with you, but for a tax return.

notes.front: What is intake at a volunteer site?
notes.back: The first process: helping the taxpayer complete Form 13614-C and assigning the return to a preparer.
notes.explanation: Only greeters, screeners and client facilitators certified in Intake/Interview and Quality Review may do this work.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2: The Intake Process”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Only Intake/Interview and Quality Review certified greeters, screeners and client facilitators can assist taxpayers in completing Form 13614-C and assign tax returns to VITA/TCE tax return preparers.
notes.example: Like a hospital’s reception and triage desk, but deciding which certified preparer should take the return.

notes.front: What is the interview at a volunteer site?
notes.back: The process in which a tax-law-certified volunteer questions the taxpayer, starting by confirming photo identification and taxpayer identification numbers.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 allows no other volunteer to interview the taxpayer.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3: The Interview Process”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Only IRS-tax law certified volunteers may interview the taxpayer. The basic steps are: Step 1: Confirm Photo Identification and Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TIN)
notes.example: Like a mechanic walking round the car with its owner before starting work, but going through a tax form with the taxpayer.

notes.front: Who is a taxpayer “known to the site”?
notes.back: One who visits the same site every year for return preparation and is known to its coordinator and volunteers.
notes.explanation: The visits must be frequent and yearly, and the taxpayer known to both the coordinator and the volunteers.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 1: Confirm Photo Identification and TIN”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: The definition of “known to the site” refers only to a taxpayer that frequently visits the same site every year for tax return preparation and is known to the site coordinator and the volunteers at the site.
notes.example: Like a regular at a village café whom the staff greet by name, but for proof of identity at a tax site.

notes.front: What is a probing question in the interview?
notes.back: A question that develops or clarifies the intake sheet and confirms the taxpayer’s information is complete and accurate.
notes.explanation: It is step 3 of the interview in Publication 5838.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 3: Interview the taxpayer”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Step 3: Interview the taxpayer Use probing questions to develop and/or clarify information on the intake sheet and to confirm the information provided by the taxpayer is complete and accurate.
notes.example: Like a journalist asking “and what happened next?”, but about a taxpayer’s income and expenses.

notes.front: What is the Global Carry Forward consent?
notes.back: The consent on page 6 of Form 13614-C (Form 15080) that lets any active volunteer site bring forward the taxpayer’s return information.
notes.explanation: It authorises the software provider to make that information available through TaxSlayer Pro Online.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Global Carry Forward Consent”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Page 6 of Form 13614-C contains the Global Carry Forward consent (Form 15080, Consent to Disclose Tax Return Information to VITA/TCE Tax Preparation Sites) that authorizes information sharing between VITA/TCE sites via TaxSlayer Pro Online. Global Carry Forward allows the software provider to make the taxpayer’s tax return information available to any active volunteer site participating in the VITA/TCE program.
notes.example: Like letting any branch of your bank see your account history, but for last year’s return at a different volunteer site.

notes.front: What are the three distinct processes behind every volunteer-prepared return?
notes.back: Intake, interview and quality review.
notes.explanation: The training adds that proper use of Form 13614-C correlates directly with preparing an accurate return.
notes.source: Publication 5101 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training, “Summary”, PDF p. 61
notes.evidence: Intake, Interview and Quality review are three distinct processes • SPEC has determined there is a direct correlation between the proper use of Form 13614-C and the preparation of an accurate tax return

notes.front: At step 2 of intake, what three things are taxpayers told they will be expected to do?
notes.back: Complete Form 13614-C first; be interviewed by the preparer; take part in a quality review by someone other than the preparer.
notes.explanation: Explaining this at the start sets out all three processes before any preparation begins.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 2”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Step 2: Explain the Intake, Interview, and Quality Review processes so that taxpayers understand that they are expected to: y Complete Form 13614-C prior to having the return prepared y Be interviewed by the return preparer and answer additional questions as needed y Participate in a quality review of their tax return by someone other than the return preparer

notes.front: A taxpayer asks why a second volunteer, not her preparer, will go over her finished return with her. Which of the three processes is this?
notes.back: A: quality review, done by someone other than the preparer.
notes.explanation: Intake tells taxpayers to expect a quality review by someone other than the return preparer.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 2”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Participate in a quality review of their tax return by someone other than the return preparer
notes.choices:
A) Quality review
B) Intake
C) Interview
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: intake is the greeting, document check, Form 13614-C and assignment. C is wrong: the interview is done by the preparer before the return is prepared.

notes.front: What are two benefits to the taxpayer of a complete intake, interview and quality review?
notes.back: Any two, among others: timely refunds; fewer amended returns; fewer notices; better understanding of the return; correct balances owed; fewer e-file rejects.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 also lists benefits to the volunteer, the site and the programme.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-1: Benefits of a Complete Intake/Interview and Quality Review”, PDF p. 4
notes.evidence: Benefits to the taxpayer y Receives timely refunds y Reduces the need for amended returns y Prevents IRS notices/contacts y Enhances taxpayer understanding of their tax return y Calculates balances owed correctly y Reduces e-file reject rates

notes.front: Form 13614-C must be fully completed for every return {{c1::before tax return preparation begins}}.
notes.back: before tax return preparation begins
notes.explanation: The training states this for every return prepared at a volunteer site.
notes.source: Publication 5101 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training, “Summary”, PDF p. 61
notes.evidence: Form 13614-C is required to be fully completed for every tax return prepared at a VITA/TCE site before tax return preparation begins

notes.front: To save time, a preparer starts keying in a taxpayer’s Form W-2 while the taxpayer is still filling in page 3 of Form 13614-C. Is that allowed?
notes.back: A: no; the preparer must be working with a completed Form 13614-C before starting input.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 tells preparers to make sure the form is complete before beginning return input.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 4: Preparing the Tax Return”, PDF p. 13
notes.evidence: Ensure you are working with a completed Form 13614-C before beginning tax return input.
notes.choices:
A) No, Form 13614-C must be completed first
B) Yes, if the quality reviewer checks page 3 later
C) Yes, for Form W-2 wages only
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are wrong: no input should begin until the preparer has a completed Form 13614-C.

notes.front: At the interview, a taxpayer has ticked a box on page 2 of Form 13614-C that does not apply. What does the volunteer do?
notes.back: Erase or cross out the box and put their initials by it.
notes.explanation: Volunteers must verify each answer on pages 1 to 3, confirming every checked box on pages 2 and 3.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “QSR #2”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Volunteers must verify each answer on pages 1 through 3. On pages 2 and 3, confirm each checked box is accurate. If a taxpayer incorrectly checked a box, erase or cross out the box and put your initials.

notes.front: Who may answer a taxpayer’s tax law questions during intake and interview?
notes.back: Only volunteers certified in tax law.
notes.explanation: The rule covers both the intake and the interview processes.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-2: Required Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training”, PDF p. 5
notes.evidence: Only tax law certified volunteers can answer tax law questions during intake and interview processes.

notes.front: A greeter certified only in Volunteer Standards of Conduct and Intake/Interview and Quality Review is asked whether a child’s summer camp counts for a credit. What should she do?
notes.back: A: pass the question to a tax-law-certified volunteer.
notes.explanation: Only tax-law-certified volunteers may answer taxpayers’ tax law questions on Form 13614-C.
notes.source: Publication 5101 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training, “Summary”, PDF p. 61
notes.evidence: Volunteers certified in Intake/Interview and Quality Review may assist taxpayers in completing Form 13614-C • Only IRS-tax law certified volunteers may answer taxpayers' questions related to tax law on Form 13614-C
notes.choices:
A) Pass it to a tax-law-certified volunteer
B) Answer it if she is confident
C) Tell the taxpayer to tick “No” and move on
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: confidence does not replace tax law certification. C is wrong: guessing the answer for the taxpayer is still answering a tax law question.

notes.front: May a partner design its own version of Form 13614-C?
notes.back: No; partners may ask additional questions, but they cannot create their own version of the form.
notes.explanation: Adding questions to the form is allowed; replacing the form is not.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Form 13614-C, Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet”, PDF p. 5
notes.evidence: Partners may ask additional questions on the Form 13614-C but cannot create their own version of this form.

notes.front: What is step 1 of the intake process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Greet the taxpayer.
notes.explanation: Introducing yourself establishes an open line of communication.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2: Intake Process, Step 1”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Step 1: Greet the taxpayer: Introduce yourself to the taxpayer to establish an open line of communication.

notes.front: What is step 2 of the intake process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Explain the intake, interview and quality review processes.
notes.explanation: Taxpayers then understand what they will be expected to do at each stage.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2: Intake Process, Step 2”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Step 2: Explain the Intake, Interview, and Quality Review processes so that taxpayers understand that they are expected to:

notes.front: What is step 3 of the intake process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Make sure the taxpayer has everything the preparer needs to prepare the return.
notes.explanation: It keeps volunteers’ and taxpayers’ time from being wasted by missing paperwork.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2: Intake Process, Step 3”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Step 3: Ensure the taxpayer has everything the tax preparer needs to prepare the tax return. This is important because it ensures the volunteer and taxpayer’s time is efficiently utilized, and the tax preparation process isn’t interrupted due to missing paperwork.

notes.front: What is step 4 of the intake process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Give the taxpayer Form 13614-C, or the nonresident alien intake sheet.
notes.explanation: Returns are more accurate when Form 13614-C is used correctly with an effective interview.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2: Intake Process, Step 4”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: IRS quality reviews indicate that tax return accuracy is improved when Form 13614-C is used correctly with an effective interview of the taxpayer.

notes.front: What is step 5 of the intake process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Determine the certification level the return needs.
notes.explanation: A greeter who passed the Intake/Interview and Quality Review test can usually decide this from the taxpayer’s answers.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2: Intake Process, Step 5”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Step 5: Determine the certification level required for the tax return A greeter who has passed the Intake/Interview and Quality Review certification test can usually determine the required certification needed for the tax return based on the questions answered on the Form 13614-C by the taxpayer.

notes.front: What is step 6 of the intake process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Assign the return to a tax-law-certified volunteer preparer.
notes.explanation: If the level cannot be determined, the volunteer must seek help first.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2: Intake Process, Step 6”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: Step 6: Assign tax return to an IRS-tax law certified volunteer preparer If the certification level of the tax return cannot be determined by the volunteer they must seek assistance to decide if the taxpayer’s return can be prepared at the site.

notes.front: An intake volunteer has greeted a taxpayer and explained the three processes. What should she do next?
notes.back: A: check that the taxpayer has everything the preparer will need.
notes.explanation: That is step 3 of intake; handing over Form 13614-C is step 4.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2: Intake Process”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Step 3: Ensure the taxpayer has everything the tax preparer needs to prepare the tax return.
notes.choices:
A) Check the taxpayer has everything the preparer needs
B) Assign the return to a preparer
C) Confirm the filing status
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: assignment is the last intake step. C is wrong: filing status is decided by a tax-law-certified volunteer in the interview.

notes.front: At intake, whose original photo identification should the volunteer make sure the taxpayer has brought?
notes.back: The taxpayer’s, and the spouse’s if married filing jointly; for a joint return, both spouses should be at the site that day.
notes.explanation: The identification is needed to prove identity to both the preparer and the quality reviewer.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 3”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Make sure the taxpayer (and spouse, if married filing jointly) has original photo identification with them to prove their identity to the return preparer and the quality reviewer. Verify both spouses are at the site that day if filing a joint tax return

notes.front: At intake, what proof of identification numbers should the taxpayer have for everyone on the return?
notes.back: Social Security cards or ITIN letters, or other acceptable verification.
notes.explanation: Other acceptable verification may stand in for the cards or letters.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 3”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Verify taxpayer has SSN cards and/or ITIN letters, or other acceptable verification, for everyone on the tax return.

notes.front: Which dependency question does the intake volunteer verify at step 3?
notes.back: Whether the taxpayer, or the spouse if married filing jointly, can be claimed on someone else’s return.
notes.explanation: It is one of the checks made at intake step 3.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 3”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Verify the taxpayer dependency question. Whether the taxpayer (and spouse, if married filing jointly) are claimed on someone else’s tax return.

notes.front: When the taxpayer hands back Form 13614-C, what should the intake volunteer check?
notes.back: For unanswered questions on page 1, and that the documents match the boxes ticked on pages 2 and 3.
notes.explanation: The volunteer then tells the taxpayer about any documents that seem to be missing.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 4”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Look for unanswered questions on page 1. Compare taxpayer documents to the selections made on pages 2 and 3 to ensure each applicable question is answered. Let the taxpayer know if any documents are missing based on their answers on these pages.

notes.front: A taxpayer has ticked “Unemployment benefits” on page 2 but brought no Form 1099-G. What should the intake volunteer do?
notes.back: A: tell the taxpayer the document seems to be missing.
notes.explanation: Intake compares documents with the boxes ticked on pages 2 and 3 and flags anything missing.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 4”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Let the taxpayer know if any documents are missing based on their answers on these pages.
notes.choices:
A) Tell the taxpayer the document seems to be missing
B) Untick the box so the form matches the documents
C) Say nothing and let the preparer find out
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: changing the taxpayer’s answers is not the intake volunteer’s job. C is wrong: intake should flag missing documents so preparation is not interrupted.

notes.front: In how many languages is Form 13614-C available?
notes.back: 23; sites should offer it in the languages of the taxpayers they serve.
notes.explanation: The translated forms can be printed from the Internal Revenue Service website.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 4”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Form 13614-C is available in 23 languages. Sites should provide the form in the languages of the taxpayers they serve. The translated forms can be printed from IRS.gov.

notes.front: Must taxpayers answer page 4 of Form 13614-C, and what goes into the software from it?
notes.back: No, page 4 is optional; input only the questions the taxpayer answered and leave the rest blank.
notes.explanation: Questions the taxpayer skips on page 4 stay blank in the software.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 4”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Page 4 of intake sheet is optional for the taxpayer to complete. Only input into the tax software the questions answered by the taxpayer and leave all unanswered questions blank in the software.

notes.front: An elderly taxpayer’s eyesight is too poor to fill in Form 13614-C. What should happen?
notes.back: A: a tax-law-certified volunteer fills it in by asking the questions and recording the answers.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 gives this response for taxpayers who cannot complete the form for any reason.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 4”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Cannot complete the form for any reason Fill out the form by asking them the questions and recording their answers.
notes.choices:
A) A tax-law-certified volunteer asks the questions and records the answers
B) The taxpayer is asked to come back with a relative
C) The preparer skips the form and works from the documents
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: the site can complete the form with the taxpayer. C is wrong: Form 13614-C is required for every return.

notes.front: A taxpayer mentions income or a life event that Form 13614-C does not list. What should a tax-law-certified volunteer do?
notes.back: Review the information and decide whether the return is within scope for the site and the volunteers’ certification levels.
notes.explanation: Items not on the form might indicate an out-of-scope return.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 4”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Have income, expenses, or life events not listed on Form Review the information and determine if the return is 13614-C, which might indicate an out-of-scope tax return within scope for the site requirements and volunteers’ certification levels.

notes.front: On pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C, what does the code (B) before a question mean?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: Pages 2 and 3 of the form identify the level each question may require.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 5”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C, as shown in below example, identify the required tax law certification level for each question. The levels are identified as B (Basic), A (Advanced), B/A (Basic/Advance), M (Military) and A/M (Advance/Military).

notes.front: On pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C, what does the code (A) before a question mean?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: Pages 2 and 3 show the tax law certification level each question may require.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 5”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C, as shown in below example, identify the required tax law certification level for each question. The levels are identified as B (Basic), A (Advanced), B/A (Basic/Advance), M (Military) and A/M (Advance/Military).

notes.front: On pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C, what does the code (B/A) before a question mean?
notes.back: Basic or Advanced, depending on the situation.
notes.explanation: The five codes are B, A, B/A, M and A/M.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 5”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C, as shown in below example, identify the required tax law certification level for each question. The levels are identified as B (Basic), A (Advanced), B/A (Basic/Advance), M (Military) and A/M (Advance/Military).

notes.front: On pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C, what does the code (M) before a question mean?
notes.back: Military.
notes.explanation: Military is one of the levels, alongside Basic and Advanced, that the codes show.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 5”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C, as shown in below example, identify the required tax law certification level for each question. The levels are identified as B (Basic), A (Advanced), B/A (Basic/Advance), M (Military) and A/M (Advance/Military).

notes.front: On pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C, what does the code (A/M) before a question mean?
notes.back: Advanced or Military.
notes.explanation: It combines two of the levels: Advanced and Military.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 5”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C, as shown in below example, identify the required tax law certification level for each question. The levels are identified as B (Basic), A (Advanced), B/A (Basic/Advance), M (Military) and A/M (Advance/Military).

notes.front: What does a B/A code next to a Form 13614-C question tell the volunteer?
notes.back: The topic may need only Basic certification in some situations and Advanced in others.
notes.explanation: For such questions Publication 5838 points to the Scope of Service chart in Publication 4012.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 5”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Certification level required for some questions depends on the issue or document the taxpayer provides. Refer to the Scope of Service chart in Publication 4012. For example: B/A next to a question means it may only require Basic tax law certification in some situations and in other situations the same topic will require Advance tax law certification.

notes.front: A taxpayer ticks “Tips” (coded B/A); all her tips are reported on her Form W-2. What level does this item need?
notes.back: A: Basic.
notes.explanation: Form 13614-C marks tips as Basic when they are reported on the Form W-2.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 2, Income”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: (B/A) Tips (B/A) Tips (Basic when reported on W2)
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Military
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: the form makes tips Basic when reported on Form W-2. C is wrong: tips are not coded M.

notes.front: Every box a taxpayer ticked is coded B except “Sale of stocks, bonds or real estate”, coded A. To whom should the return be assigned?
notes.back: A: a preparer certified at the Advanced level or above.
notes.explanation: Returns go to preparers certified at or above the level the return requires, and one Advanced item sets that level.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 6”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: Every site is required to have a process for assigning taxpayers to volunteer preparers who are certified at or above the level required to prepare their return.
notes.choices:
A) A preparer certified at Advanced or above
B) A Basic preparer, since most items are Basic
C) Any preparer, with an Advanced quality reviewer
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: the level is set by the item that needs the highest certification. C is wrong: the preparer must be certified at or above the level of the return.

notes.front: What process must every site have for assigning returns?
notes.back: One that assigns taxpayers to preparers certified at or above the level their return requires.
notes.explanation: Sites may show volunteers’ levels with badges, stickers, nameplates or the optional Form 14509.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 6”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: Every site is required to have a process for assigning taxpayers to volunteer preparers who are certified at or above the level required to prepare their return. The method for identifying certification levels of volunteers can include indicators on name badges, stickers, nameplates, or other partner-created products.

notes.front: If the volunteer cannot tell what certification level a return needs, what happens?
notes.back: They seek help; the decision rests on the site’s return preparation policy and the Scope of Service chart.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 says this ensures taxpayers are not mistakenly turned away.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 6”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: The final decision will be based on a combination of the site’s return preparation policy and Scope of Service chart listed in Publication 4012. This ensures taxpayers are not mistakenly turned away from the site.

notes.front: Which certification test must greeters, screeners and client facilitators pass before they help with Form 13614-C or assign returns?
notes.back: The Intake/Interview and Quality Review certification test.
notes.explanation: It applies to anyone who helps complete Form 13614-C or assigns returns.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-2: Required Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training”, PDF p. 4
notes.evidence: greeters, screeners and client facilitators who assist taxpayers in completing Form 13614-C, or assign tax returns to VITA/TCE preparers must pass the Intake/ Interview and Quality Review certification test.

notes.front: A new receptionist has passed only the Volunteer Standards of Conduct test. The site is busy and she offers to hand out returns to preparers. May she?
notes.back: A: no; only greeters certified in Intake/Interview and Quality Review may assign returns.
notes.explanation: Assigning returns is an intake task reserved for greeters certified in Intake/Interview and Quality Review.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2: The Intake Process”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Only Intake/Interview and Quality Review certified greeters, screeners and client facilitators can assist taxpayers in completing Form 13614-C and assign tax returns to VITA/TCE tax return preparers.
notes.choices:
A) No, not without Intake/Interview and Quality Review certification
B) Yes, assigning returns needs no certification
C) Yes, if a preparer checks each assignment
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: assigning returns requires Intake/Interview and Quality Review certification. C is wrong: supervision does not replace the certification.

notes.front: If a return is outside the scope of the volunteer programme, what should the volunteer tell the taxpayer?
notes.back: To seek help from a professional preparer, without suggesting any particular one.
notes.explanation: Naming a preparer, especially one linked to a volunteer or the site, would be a conflict of interest.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-4: VITA/TCE Program Scope of Service”, PDF p. 6
notes.evidence: If the return is not within the scope of VITA/TCE, explain to the taxpayer they must seek assistance from a professional preparer. Avoid a conflict of interest by not suggesting any specific professional preparer. This includes professional preparers associated with a volunteer, any other specific individual, or organization connected to the VITA/TCE site.

notes.front: A taxpayer’s return is out of scope. He asks the volunteer for a name, and her brother-in-law is a paid preparer nearby. What should she say?
notes.back: A: that he must see a professional preparer, without recommending any particular one.
notes.explanation: Suggesting a preparer associated with a volunteer is the conflict of interest Publication 5838 warns against.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-4: VITA/TCE Program Scope of Service”, PDF p. 6
notes.evidence: Avoid a conflict of interest by not suggesting any specific professional preparer. This includes professional preparers associated with a volunteer
notes.choices:
A) See a professional preparer, with no specific name
B) Recommend her brother-in-law, since he is qualified
C) Prepare it anyway to avoid sending him elsewhere
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: that is the conflict of interest the handbook forbids. C is wrong: out-of-scope returns must not be prepared.

notes.front: A return is within the programme’s scope but above the volunteer’s certification level. Where should the taxpayer be referred?
notes.back: To another tax-law-certified volunteer with the right level, or to another site that prepares returns at that level.
notes.explanation: The referral stays within the programme, to a volunteer or site certified at the level needed.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-4: VITA/TCE Program Scope of Service”, PDF p. 6
notes.evidence: If the tax return does not fall within the volunteer’s certification level, refer the taxpayer to another IRS-tax law certified volunteer preparer with the appropriate certification level or to another site that prepares returns at that certification level.

notes.front: A taxpayer wants a return prepared for an earlier year. Which Form 13614-C must be completed?
notes.back: One current-year Form 13614-C for each prior-year return.
notes.explanation: The current-year form is used to decide the scope and certification level of each prior-year return.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Prior year returns”, PDF p. 347
notes.evidence: A current year Form 13614-C must be completed for each prior year return and will be used to determine the scope and certification level of each return.

notes.front: What is step 1 of the interview process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Confirm photo identification and taxpayer identification numbers.
notes.explanation: The rules for acceptable documents are those in Publication 4299.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3: Interview Process, Step 1”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Step 1: Confirm Photo Identification and Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TIN) Verify the identity of the taxpayer (and spouse, if married filing jointly) using an original government-issued photo ID and confirm Social Security numbers (SSN) or individual taxpayer identification numbers (ITIN) according to rules listed in Publication 4299

notes.front: What is step 2 of the interview process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Review Form 13614-C.
notes.explanation: It starts by making sure the taxpayer answered every question on page 1.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3: Interview Process, Step 2”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Step 2: Review Form 13614-C Ensure the taxpayer answered all questions on Form 13614-C, page 1.

notes.front: What is step 3 of the interview process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Interview the taxpayer, using probing questions.
notes.explanation: This develops or clarifies the intake sheet and confirms the information is complete and accurate.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3: Interview Process, Step 3”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Step 3: Interview the taxpayer Use probing questions to develop and/or clarify information on the intake sheet

notes.front: What is step 4 of the interview process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Make the filing status and dependency determinations.
notes.explanation: Volunteers use the resource tools in Publication 4012 for these decisions.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3: Interview Process, Step 4”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Step 4: Make filing status and dependency determinations Use the resource tools in Publication 4012 when determining taxpayer filing status and eligible dependents to be claimed.

notes.front: What is step 5 of the interview process in Publication 5838?
notes.back: Review the documentation.
notes.explanation: The preparer looks at every supporting document, such as Forms W-2 and 1099 and payment receipts.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3: Interview Process, Step 5”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Step 5: Review documentation Look at all supporting documentation provided by the taxpayer (Forms W-2, 1099, payment receipts, etc.).

notes.front: A preparer begins by asking a new taxpayer about her children’s school fees before seeing any identification. Which interview step has she skipped?
notes.back: A: step 1, confirming photo identification and taxpayer identification numbers.
notes.explanation: The interview starts by verifying identity and numbers before the form and questions.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3: Interview Process, Step 1”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Only IRS-tax law certified volunteers may interview the taxpayer. The basic steps are: Step 1: Confirm Photo Identification and Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TIN)
notes.choices:
A) Step 1, confirming identification and numbers
B) Step 4, filing status and dependency
C) None; the order does not matter
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: that decision comes later and is not what was skipped. C is wrong: the handbook lists identification as the first step.

notes.front: Who may approve a “known to the site” exception?
notes.back: Only the site coordinator.
notes.explanation: Each site sets its own process for getting the coordinator’s approval.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 1”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Only the site coordinator has the authority to approve these exceptions. Each site determines the process for obtaining a Site Coordinator’s approval of a “known to the site” exception.

notes.front: Mr Osei had his return prepared at this site once, last year. He forgot his identification, and the coordinator does not know him. Is he “known to the site”?
notes.back: A: no; one earlier return does not make a taxpayer known to the site.
notes.explanation: Being prepared at a site in a prior year does not automatically qualify, and he is not known to the coordinator.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 1”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Just because a taxpayer’s return was prepared at a site in a prior year, it does not automatically qualify as “known to the site”.
notes.choices:
A) No, one earlier visit does not qualify him
B) Yes, because his return is in last year’s records
C) Yes, if the preparer who helped him last year vouches for him
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: a prior-year return alone does not qualify. C is wrong: only the site coordinator can approve the exception.

notes.front: Mrs Diaz has come to the same site every year for a decade and the coordinator knows her well. She forgot her grandson’s Social Security card. What may happen?
notes.back: A: the site coordinator may approve a known-to-the-site exception for the proof of number.
notes.explanation: The coordinator has discretion to waive proof of a taxpayer identification number for a taxpayer known to the site.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 1”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: The site coordinator has the discretion to grant an exception to the requirement to provide a valid form of identification and/or the requirement to provide proof of taxpayer identification number if the taxpayer is known to the site.
notes.choices:
A) The site coordinator may approve an exception
B) Her preparer may waive the card because she is a regular
C) Nothing: no exception exists for a missing card
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: only the site coordinator can approve it. C is wrong: the exception can cover proof of taxpayer identification numbers.

notes.front: How does a taxpayer “known to the site” differ from one whose return the site simply prepared before?
notes.back: Known to the site means a frequent yearly visitor known to the coordinator and volunteers; a past return alone does not qualify.
notes.explanation: Only the first can be granted the identification exception, and only by the site coordinator.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 1”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Just because a taxpayer’s return was prepared at a site in a prior year, it does not automatically qualify as “known to the site”. Only the site coordinator has the authority to approve these exceptions.

notes.front: Who completes the gray shaded areas of Form 13614-C headed “To be completed by certified volunteer”, and when?
notes.back: The preparer, during the interview with the taxpayer.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 places this during the interview with the taxpayer.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 2”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Preparer will complete the gray shaded areas on the form titled “To be completed by certified volunteer” during interview with taxpayer.

notes.front: A taxpayer has written “Y” in the gray “To be completed by certified volunteer” columns for her son. What should the preparer do?
notes.back: A: go through those questions with her in the interview and complete the gray area himself.
notes.explanation: The gray areas are for the preparer to complete during the interview, not for the taxpayer.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 4”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: On Form 13614-C complete the gray shaded area titled: To be completed by certified volunteer. The answers to the questions asked will provide the information needed to make tax law determinations for dependency, filing status, and qualified tax credits.
notes.choices:
A) Go through the questions with her and complete the gray area
B) Accept her “Y” answers as they stand
C) Leave the gray area for the quality reviewer
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: the preparer must ask the questions and complete the area. C is wrong: the preparer completes it during the interview, before preparation.

notes.front: How does the preparer show that a question the taxpayer left unticked was discussed and does not apply?
notes.back: By writing “No”, “N/A”, a check mark or another marking next to it.
notes.explanation: The marking records that the question was discussed with the taxpayer.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 2”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: If a question does not apply to the taxpayer, write “No”, “N/A”, a check mark, or other markings next to the question. This will indicate that the question does not apply but has been discussed with the taxpayer.

notes.front: The quality reviewer sees that the “Alimony” question on page 2 is blank, with no mark at all. What does that suggest?
notes.back: A: there is no sign the preparer discussed it with the taxpayer; it should have been marked “No”, “N/A” or similar.
notes.explanation: Every unchecked question must be addressed and marked to show it was discussed.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 2”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: All unchecked boxes on pages 1 through 3 of the form must be addressed.
notes.choices:
A) No sign it was discussed; it should be marked
B) Alimony does not apply, so nothing is needed
C) The taxpayer must fill in page 2 again
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: a blank does not show the question was discussed. C is wrong: the preparer addresses unchecked questions with the taxpayer; the form is not redone.

notes.front: On page 1 of Form 13614-C, which date does a divorced taxpayer give?
notes.back: The date of the final decree.
notes.explanation: It is one of three marital statuses on page 1 that come with a date box.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 1, marital status”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: Divorced Legally Separated but not Divorced Widowed Date of final decree Date of separate maintenance decree Year of spouse’s death

notes.front: On page 1 of Form 13614-C, what does a widowed taxpayer give, and what does a legally separated one give?
notes.back: Widowed: the year of the spouse’s death. Legally separated: the date of the separate maintenance decree.
notes.explanation: Form 13614-C has a separate date box for each of these statuses, and one for divorce.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 1, marital status”, PDF p. 1
notes.evidence: Divorced Legally Separated but not Divorced Widowed Date of final decree Date of separate maintenance decree Year of spouse’s death

notes.front: What kind of question does Publication 5838 suggest in the interview instead of simple yes/no questions?
notes.back: Open-ended questions.
notes.explanation: Its example contrasts “Tell me about the interest on your bank account” with a yes/no version.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 3”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Consider using open-ended questions (“Tell me about the interest on your bank account”) rather than simple yes/no questions (“Do you have interest on your bank account?”).

notes.front: Which question best follows Publication 5838’s advice for asking about a taxpayer’s work last year?
notes.back: A: “Tell me about the jobs you had last year.”
notes.explanation: An open-ended question invites the taxpayer to describe everything, not just answer yes or no.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 3”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Consider using open-ended questions (“Tell me about the interest on your bank account”) rather than simple yes/no questions
notes.choices:
A) “Tell me about the jobs you had last year.”
B) “Did you have a job last year?”
C) “You only had one job, right?”
notes.choicesExplained: B is a simple yes/no question. C is a yes/no question that also suggests the answer.

notes.front: When must errors or omissions found during the interview be corrected on Form 13614-C?
notes.back: Before tax return preparation starts.
notes.explanation: Preparers also note on the form any answers that change or information the form did not capture.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 3”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Notate comments when taxpayers answers change or taxpayers provide additional information not captured on Form 13614-C Errors or omissions of information identified during the interview with the taxpayer must be corrected or entered on the Form 13614-C prior to tax return preparation.

notes.front: In the interview a taxpayer mentions a second job she forgot to tick on page 2. What should the preparer do before preparing the return?
notes.back: A: correct Form 13614-C to include it before preparing the return.
notes.explanation: Omissions found in the interview must be entered on the form before preparation.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 3”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Errors or omissions of information identified during the interview with the taxpayer must be corrected or entered on the Form 13614-C prior to tax return preparation.
notes.choices:
A) Correct Form 13614-C and note the change first
B) Just include the job in the return
C) Tell the quality reviewer about it verbally
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are wrong: the correction must be on Form 13614-C before preparation, not only in the return or in conversation.

notes.front: For people listed on page 1, how many gray-area questions must be answered?
notes.back: All of them for anyone claimed on the return; only the disqualifying ones for anyone not claimed.
notes.explanation: Anyone not claimed needs only the questions that could rule them out.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 4”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: If any of these individuals are claimed on the tax return, then all questions must be answered. y If someone is not claimed on the return, then only disqualifying question(s) must be answered.

notes.front: The return shows income that needs no source document and the taxpayer provided none. What does the preparer do?
notes.back: Note the information on Form 13614-C in the Additional Notes/Comments section.
notes.explanation: It applies to income or expenses that need no source document when none was provided.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 3, Step 5”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: If the taxpayer has income or expenses listed on the return that do not require a source document and none were provided, notate information on Form 13614-C in Additional Notes/Comments section.

notes.front: While preparing the return, a preparer finds a document that contradicts Form 13614-C. How is the form corrected?
notes.back: Line through the incorrect information, correct it and add notes on the form.
notes.explanation: The quality reviewer then has the most current information.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 4: Preparing the Tax Return”, PDF p. 13
notes.evidence: line through incorrect information on Form 13614-C and make corrections along with adding notes on the form so quality reviewer has the most current information.

notes.front: What must happen before a preparer enters a taxpayer’s Global Carry Forward consent PIN and date in the software?
notes.back: The taxpayer must sign and date a paper consent form.
notes.explanation: Without a signed paper consent, the taxpayer must enter their own PIN.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Global Carry Forward Consent”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: then the taxpayer must enter his or her own PIN in the tax preparation software. Based on IRC 7216, if the return preparer is entering the consent PIN and date into the tax preparation software, the taxpayer must sign and date a paper consent form before you enter the consent PIN and date.

notes.front: A taxpayer grants Global Carry Forward consent this year. Next year she goes to a different volunteer site that uses TaxSlayer. What happens?
notes.back: A: her return populates with the prior-year data, whichever volunteer site filed it.
notes.explanation: That is the purpose of the consent: sharing the return information with any active volunteer site.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Global Carry Forward Consent”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: If consent is granted, the tax return populates with their prior year data, regardless of which VITA/TCE site filed their tax return previously.
notes.choices:
A) Her return populates with last year’s data
B) Nothing, since the data stays with the first site
C) She must bring a copy of last year’s return to unlock it
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: the consent is what lets other sites see the data. C is wrong: the data is carried forward in the software.

notes.front: Does refusing the Global Carry Forward consent affect the service the taxpayer receives?
notes.back: No; granting or denying it has no effect on the service during the visit.
notes.explanation: It is the taxpayer’s free choice either way.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Global Carry Forward Consent”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Whether the taxpayer decides to grant or deny Global Carry Forward, it has no effect on the service they receive during their visit to the site.

notes.front: During intake and interview, what may only a tax-law-certified volunteer do with tax information, as opposed to an intake-certified greeter?
notes.back: Review, correct or clarify tax-related information; the greeter helps complete Form 13614-C and assigns returns.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 reserves the tax-related work for volunteers certified in tax law.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 2, Step 3”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: During the intake and interview process, only an IRS-tax law certified volunteer can review, correct, and/or clarify tax related information.
